text_clean:
[Product: Alphasonik CHARM Wireless Bluetooth Portable Speaker with Digital LED Alarm Clock, Auto and Manual Dimmer, FM Radio, HD Sound and Bass, Micro USB, Auxilliary 3.5mm, SD card, for iPhone and Samsung | ASIN: B008R523N2] For all those complaining about the low volume level or lack of bass depth, and then comparing it to your home docks or the big Jambox or the Bose you are judging this unit in an unreasonable way. This speaker was meant to be used on the go...whether it be outside by the pool, in the bathroom as a shower companion, or at the beach... or maybe bedside. It is designed to replace the speaker on your cell phone or tablet while watching videos or streaming music, and it does that exceedingly well.

It puts out about as much volume as a decent small boombox or high end (not Bang and Olufson or Bose high end... think $70-$100 range) This thing's biggest strength, however, is not it is volume level, but the quality of the sound. It is very clean, crisp, and distortion free...even at full volume. but how can it be when your left and right speakers are 2 inches apart? The bass does not vibrate your chest cavity, but it is not designed to... it does, however, have enough bass response that you can actually hear the bass lines (free of rattling or distortion), which is something not often found in speakers this size or even 50% larger than this size.

It is very easy to use, and syncs flawlessly. The case is rugged, and the base does not suffer from the same problem that plagues the jambox (it will not slide off your table at high volumes).

If you want an easily portable, wireless speaker with an amazing sound-to-size ratio that you can carry around with you everywhere, and you are more concerned with sound quality than sheer volume, I have yet to find anything else in this price range (around $150) or form factor (small enough to throw in cargo short pockets or a small bag) that can beat the Solemate.

I recently purchased several bluetooth speakers to test in my bedroom and office in hopes that I would like one enough to keep. Before I get into the details, I will cut to the chase and let you know that I decided to keep the Big Jambox over the Bose SoundLink. While the Bose puts out a truly impressive amount of sound from such a small, portable package, the sound quality is not as good as the Big Jambox at low to normal volume levels.

The products I tested were the Bose SoundLink Wireless, Jawbone Jambox, Jawbone Big Jambox, and Logitech Wireless Boombox. Ultimately, though, I felt that the Big Jambox sounded and looked better (for my taste), so I returned the Bose and Logitech Wireless Boombox (I also kept the little Jambox for my office, which does not sound nearly as good as the bigger speakers, but makes for a great ultra-portable speaker for half the price ($150)).

My biggest problem with the sound of the Bose Soundlink is that there is far too much bass at low to normal volume levels. This is a problem for me because the bass clouds the rest of the music -- vocals become difficult to hear and the treble is nearly non-existent. The Bose sounds muddy and veiled under these circumstances, especially in small rooms. And to be clear, I am a big fan of bass. I hate speakers that have no bass because the music I listen to (jazz, pop, hip hop, electronic) really benefit from bass. In contrast, the Big Jambox has a much better balance of bass, midrange, and treble at low to normal volume levels, providing a clearer overall sound.*

However, this is only an issue when the volume on the Bose is lower. As you turn the volume up, the bass becomes less pronounced, as if the other frequencies get louder but the bass stays at the same level. It sounds much much better when the volume is cranked up. In fact, I would say the Bose sounds significantly better than the Big Jambox at high volumes -- at their loudest settings, the Bose projects a bigger, richer sound than the Big Jambox, which can sound a bit shrill and boxed in at its higher settings. The "better" speaker ultimately comes down to how loud you listen to music.

This is not to say that the Big Jambox sounds bad at high volumes. Frankly, I do not think anyone relying on a small wireless speaker is expecting perfection. The Big Jambox can still fill a very large room with an impressive amount of sound, and I find that it tends to distort less at higher volumes than the Bose. Ultimately, I preferred the sound of the Big Jambox for my use and decided to keep that speaker. If you are more of a party-level listener, though, you would be wise to choose differently.

*One issue I have had with the Big Jambox is that, unlike the Bose, the Big Jambox emits a static "hissing" sound that is audible in a quiet room. If you listen to music at low volume or sit near the speaker, this sound will be very obvious (and possibly quite annoying). The Bose has no hiss sound whatsoever. I am hoping this is an issue Jawbone can fix with a firmware update, as they did with the little Jambox, but it is not much of an issue for me since I listen at normal volumes and never sit near the speaker.
